name: Peptides for bone growth

card.summary: Growth-hormone-releasing and repair peptide stacks that some people discuss as a way to build bone density or size for a stronger frame and jaw.
card.note: Research compounds that are not approved for this use; growth-axis stimulation has documented risks.

quick.overview:
Some looksmaxxing forum members discuss peptide stacks, such as growth hormone secretagogues (CJC-1295, ipamorelin, GHRPs), IGF-1 derivatives and thymosin peptides, as ways to support bone growth. The appearance idea is a larger or denser skeleton, for example a broader frame or stronger facial bone structure.

Human research on anabolic peptides for bone relates to osteoporosis, where review literature examines short peptides that stimulate bone formation. Growth hormone has also been tested for bone in conditions such as anorexia nervosa, obesity and pediatric osteoporosis. Whether peptide stacks change bone in healthy adults has not been tested in trials.
quick.how: On forums the peptides are described as injectables bought from research-chemical suppliers and combined in stacks. They are not approved for bone growth. No protocol details are provided here.
quick.risks: These compounds are sold as research peptides and are not approved medicines for this use. Growth-axis stimulation can enlarge tissues and affect glucose; a forum reply to the thread notes cancer worries, and another advises an X-ray first, referring to growth plate status. Ipamorelin is on the World Anti-Doping Agency prohibited list.[2]

lead: Peptides for bone growth is a forum term for stacks of research peptides that people discuss using to increase bone mass or size. Thread posts list growth hormone secretagogues such as CJC-1295, ipamorelin, GHRP-2 and GHRP-6 and tesamorelin, IGF-1 variants such as LR3 and DES, and thymosins like TB-500, describing effects on muscle, fat loss, recovery and tissue repair.[1]

The appearance rationale is that more bone would mean a broader skeleton or stronger facial structure. One reply in the thread said that users in their late teens or older should get an X-ray first, a reference to whether growth plates remain open.[1]

Scientific literature on anabolic peptides concerns bone loss. A 2016 review in Medicinal Research Reviews describes short anabolic peptides for bone growth in the context of osteoporosis, a skeletal disorder with high fracture costs.[3]

chain: Growth-axis peptides raise GH or IGF-1 signalling
Claimed denser or larger skeleton and stronger-looking frame
angle.text: Users hope the peptides add bone, giving a more robust frame or jaw. The mechanism is claimed on the basis of growth hormone pathways, not demonstrated in healthy adults.

infobox: CJC-1295, ipamorelin, GHRPs, IGF-1 LR3, TB-500

paras: A looksmax.org guide groups the peptides into growth hormone secretagogues, IGF derivatives and thymosins. It credits them with muscle growth, fat loss, recovery and tissue repair.[1] Other members replied with concern about cancer risk and with the recommendation to check growth plates first.[1]

Ipamorelin is a pentapeptide, a selective agonist of the ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor originally developed by Novo Nordisk. It raises growth hormone in animals and humans without raising cortisol or prolactin, has a half-life of about two hours, and in rats has been linked to longitudinal bone growth.[2] Helsinn tested it in phase II trials for postoperative ileus and discontinued development due to lack of efficacy.[2]

No studies found testing these peptide stacks for bone growth in healthy people. Related research includes registered growth hormone trials for bone: in anorexia nervosa (NCT00283595), in obesity (NCT01724489), in pediatric osteoporosis (NCT00757393), and with testosterone for bone loss in men with hypopituitarism (NCT00080483).[4][5][6][7] A 2016 review covers short anabolic peptides for osteoporosis.[3]
Ipamorelin is not an approved drug and is marketed mainly as a research peptide; it is on the WADA prohibited list.[2] Forum members raise cancer concerns about growth stimulation.[1]

lore.intro: The topic appears on looksmax.org as a long guide to peptide classes and as part of wider discussion of growth hormone and height or bone changes.[1]

claims.claim: Peptide stacks can promote bone growth
claims.believers: Thread authors list GH secretagogues, IGF derivatives and thymosins as supporting growth, recovery and repair.[1]
claims.experts: No published trial has tested these stacks for bone growth in healthy adults; research on short anabolic peptides concerns osteoporosis.[3]

claims.claim: Growth hormone secretagogues stimulate bone in animals
claims.believers: Users cite GH-axis stimulation as a mechanism for bone changes.[1]
claims.experts: Ipamorelin has been linked to longitudinal bone growth in rats and raises GH in humans, but it did not show efficacy in its phase II trial for ileus.[2]
